newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS confirms CP ratings, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: CBRS confirms CP ratings, outlook stable.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it maintained the credit ratings assigned to Canadian Pacific Ltd's short- and long-term debt securities at A-1 (Low) and A (Low), respectively, with a stable outlook.

CBRS said the good quality rating on CP's C$1.0 billion commercial paper program, debentures and notes reflects the diversity and the strong competitive position of its various businesses which hold a pre-eminent position in major sectors of the Canadian economy.

The positive effects of asset rationalization, started in 1993, the strengthening of core competencies in various businesses and the benefits of an improving economy in North America all contributed to a record performance and strengthening of CP's credit profile, CBRS said.

It said CP's financial performance in 1996 represents a dramatic reversal of fortune as it engineered a C$1.5 billion turnaround in operating income and C$267.1 million improvement improvement in income from continuing operations before unusual items. In 1995, CP's massive restructuring charges of C$1.1 billion had triggered a net loss of C$823.5 million.
In 1996 there was significant improvement in all sectors, and net income reached C$829.1 million, CBRS said.
From a credit perspective, the significant boost in CP's cash low and the sale of Marathon (including the elimination of associated debt) enabled CP to reduce its corporate debt by C$1,759 million.
At the end off 1996, CP's net debt-to-equity position was reduced to 29 percent from year earlier 41 percent and its coverage ratio improved to a solid 5.8X from a negative position a year ago.

CBRS said the credit outlook reflected more significant progress in CP's major business sectors in 1997. The bond rating service said it anticipated the strong business position of CPR to continue in Western Canada.
Further benefits were expected to be realized if CP maintained a healthy labor climate and returned its eastern rail operations to profitability, CBRS said.
Similarly, the energy and hospitality sectors were expected to show a steady performance through moderate increases in earnings and cash flow in 1997.

CBRS said CP and its subsidiaries' product portfolios had become moderately less susceptible to cyclical swings and that further progress in operating procedures and efficiency should maintain the positive momentum built in 1995-96.
